examined_formations.title: GOOGLE_CONTENT_API_TO_MERCHANT_API_MIGRATION
examined_formations.chinese_title: Google Shopping Content API迁移工厂
examined_formations.state_change: Content API for Shopping sunset on 18 August 2026; from 1 September non-extended calls can intermittently fail with HTTP 410 and full decommissioning is planned for early 2027.
examined_formations.operational_cost: Broken custom integrations can interrupt product listing/account-management workflows tied to commerce.
examined_formations.existing_budget_signal: Affected custom integrations are maintained software; third-party commerce platforms already maintain migration on behalf of their customers.
examined_formations.machine_delivery: Google publishes detailed method/resource compatibility guides, making much code transformation deterministic.
examined_formations.control_surface: For merchants on third-party platforms the platform partner owns the migration; custom integrations remain customer-specific source-code changes.

examined_formations.title: CLOUDFLARE_SERVICE_KEY_TO_API_TOKEN_MIGRATION
examined_formations.state_change: Service Key authentication is scheduled for removal on 30 September 2026.
examined_formations.operational_cost: Integrations that keep X-Auth-User-Service-Key can fail after the deadline.
examined_formations.existing_budget_signal: The affected integrations already run in customer infrastructure, but no distinct paid migration role is evidenced.
examined_formations.machine_delivery: Replacement is a well-documented API Token with scoped permissions; many cases reduce to credential/configuration updates.
examined_formations.control_surface: Customer-controlled code and credentials; no separate cross-customer asset forms from performing the change.

examined_formations.title: SCHIPHOL_API_PLATFORM_JWT_MIGRATION
examined_formations.state_change: Schiphol's legacy API platform is scheduled to shut down on 1 October 2026; legacy API-key integrations must move to new endpoint prefixes and OAuth 2.0/JWT.
examined_formations.operational_cost: Unmigrated integrations stop working after the shutdown.
examined_formations.existing_budget_signal: API consumers have existing integration maintenance, but the ecosystem is bounded and no independent repeated payer rail is established.
examined_formations.machine_delivery: The platform provides exact endpoint/authentication migration instructions and code-oriented guidance.
examined_formations.control_surface: Schiphol itself provides migration support and office hours; access approval and credentials remain platform controlled.

examined_formations.title: BOOKING_HOTELPRODUCTNOTIF_V13_MIGRATION
examined_formations.state_change: Older GET v1.0-v1.2 and POST v1.0 OTA_HotelProductNotif versions sunset on 1 September 2026.
examined_formations.operational_cost: Explicit old-version calls return unsupported-version errors after sunset.
examined_formations.existing_budget_signal: Connectivity Partners already own and maintain the integration as part of their platform relationship.
examined_formations.machine_delivery: Booking.com publishes version comparison and migration guidance; some unversioned calls are automatically routed to v1.3.
examined_formations.control_surface: The value loop is internal to existing Connectivity Partners rather than an unowned third-party operator surface.

examined_formations.title: AZURE_ANOMALY_DETECTOR_RETIREMENT_REPLACEMENT
examined_formations.state_change: Azure Anomaly Detector retires on 1 October 2026.
examined_formations.operational_cost: Applications dependent on the managed API need another anomaly-detection path to preserve functionality.
examined_formations.existing_budget_signal: Existing paid Azure usage demonstrates deployed demand for the function.
examined_formations.machine_delivery: A replacement can be API-shaped and low-friction.
examined_formations.control_surface: Exact drop-in replacement products already market near-schema-compatible migration, while Microsoft documents alternative paths.

examined_formations.title: SALESFORCE_ESSENTIALS_TO_PRO_SUITE_MIGRATION
examined_formations.state_change: Salesforce announced Essentials retirement in 2026 with consent/end-of-renewal milestones and support ending 18 September 2026.
examined_formations.operational_cost: Organizations that do not consent/upgrade can lose access to the Essentials org.
examined_formations.existing_budget_signal: Existing Salesforce subscriptions are explicit software budget.
examined_formations.machine_delivery: Much of the transition is a Salesforce-controlled edition upgrade with a native migration guide.
examined_formations.control_surface: Salesforce owns the destination, entitlement, consent flow and upgrade process.
